defenses.title: Missing explicit error taxonomy across auth/session/data/privacy boundaries
defenses.existing_state_justification: A strict shared taxonomy has not been required to ship current features because boundaries already provide local handling patterns (provider guards, route status codes, service-level catches) and the system remains operable without a global discriminated union.

defenses.title: Silent-failure risk from multi-layer fallback chains (crypto + cache + offline)
defenses.existing_state_justification: Fallback chains are an intentional resilience strategy to prioritize continuity when network, storage, or crypto dependencies are unstable. In this context, graceful degradation is preferable to hard failure for user-facing reliability.

defenses.title: Inconsistent error propagation between client provider, service facades, and API routes
defenses.existing_state_justification: Propagation differs because each layer serves a different contract (UI ergonomics, service composition, HTTP semantics). Some variation is expected while the architecture is still converging.

defenses.title: Import/export pipeline likely lacks partial-failure semantics
defenses.existing_state_justification: The current import path appears optimized for whole-operation success to keep behavior predictable for users, and adding detailed partial-failure reporting may have been deferred until higher data volumes or conflict rates justify the complexity.

defenses.title: Unused dual-service architecture (`simple` vs `cached`) increases error drift
defenses.existing_state_justification: Maintaining both facades provides a controlled migration surface and allows experimentation with cache strategy without destabilizing the primary data path; this can be a valid interim architecture.

defenses.title: Auth refresh/validation loop lacks explicit retry budget and terminal states
defenses.existing_state_justification: Auth control flow can remain safe without a fully formalized state machine when guard conditions and session checks already gate refresh behavior; explicit budgeting is beneficial but not always mandatory early.

defenses.title: Cache subsystem breadth can mask cache-write/cache-invalidate failures
defenses.existing_state_justification: A broad cache surface is often necessary to cover heterogeneous read/write paths, and cache errors are frequently treated as non-fatal by design so core data correctness remains anchored to authoritative backend state.

defenses.title: SSR mock cache adapters risk diverging failure semantics from browser runtime
defenses.existing_state_justification: SSR adapters are expected to be simpler than browser adapters because runtime capabilities differ; parity is useful but exact failure-semantic equivalence is not always practical or required.

defenses.title: "Class + singleton + bound exports" obscures ownership of throw/catch boundaries
defenses.existing_state_justification: This structure may reflect legacy compatibility and gradual refactoring constraints rather than unnecessary complexity. It can preserve stable callsites while internals evolve.

defenses.title: Placeholder options/no-op API paths can imply successful handling when none occurred
defenses.existing_state_justification: Placeholder/no-op paths can be valid compatibility shims during phased rollout; however, they require explicit signaling to avoid false assumptions by callers.

defenses.title: Cache invalidation rule set includes non-active operations, diluting failure signal clarity
defenses.existing_state_justification: Predeclaring rules for near-term operations can reduce future integration friction, but if non-active branches materially reduce observability they should be trimmed or annotated.
